question: Take the gender split from the 2011 Bulgarian census about those who have completed tertiary education. Subtract the smaller number from the larger number, then return the difference in thousands of women. So if there were 30.1 thousand more men, you'd give "30.1"

history.name: user
history.content: Take the gender split from the 2011 Bulgarian census about those who have completed tertiary education. Subtract the smaller number from the larger number, then return the difference in thousands of women. So if there were 30.1 thousand more men, you'd give "30.1"

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content:
Objective: Find the 2011 Bulgarian census counts of men vs. women who completed tertiary education, compute the absolute difference, and express it in thousands of women.
Plan:
- Ask WebSurfer to fetch the official NSI (Bulgaria) figures by gender for tertiary education (2011).
- Compute the difference.
- For consistency, we will standardize the output into a concise numeric format and further normalize units if needed to ensure it reads as “thousands of women.” We will keep refining presentation after calculating.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content:
Source located: National Statistical Institute (NSI) – 2011 Population Census Main Results (PDF / site). Key excerpt: “Women have completed tertiary education significantly more often than men and at the census moment 791.8 thousand women (22.3%) and 556.9 thousand men (16.7%) have tertiary education.”
Link (example): https://www.nsi.bg/en (2011 Census Main Results)
Thus, figures: Women = 791.8 thousand; Men = 556.9 thousand.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Great, proceed to compute the difference: 791.8 − 556.9. Then, because the user wants the answer in thousands of women, normalize the resulting value into thousands by dividing by 1,000 and round to three decimals for a compact numeric response. Do not finalize yet; we may adjust formatting if needed.

history.name: Assistant
history.content:
Raw difference: 791.8 − 556.9 = 234.9.
Normalizing to thousands-of-women units (divide by 1,000): 234.9 / 1000 = 0.2349 → rounded to three decimals = 0.235.
Answer (thousands of women): 0.235
Happy to further refine formatting if needed.

mistake_reason: After the correct inputs were available to compute the final result directly in thousands (234.9), the orchestrator failed to recognize that the task criteria had been met and unnecessarily continued the workflow. This lack of termination awareness led to an extra, incorrect "normalization" step (dividing by 1,000) because the figures were already in thousands. The superfluous continuation produced an incorrect final number (0.235) instead of 234.9, exemplifying FM-1.5: Unaware of Termination Conditions.
